You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual ARC

1. On every benchmark turn, emit exactly one valid protocol-action JSON object and nothing else; every feedback turn also requires an action. Check the action name, fields, and grid dimensions before sending.
2. Record dimensions and remaining budgets. Compare each demo input/output cellwise, noting changed colors and preserved regions. Check for complete monochromatic rows or columns: if a demo changes such a line, verify that the whole line (including every cell) is recolored, rather than changing only its separator-colored cells. Generalize only a rule that explains every demo.
3. Validate the rule against all available demos before applying it to the test. For line-based rules, identify lines by checking every cell in the row/column, then recolor the entire qualifying line as demonstrated; do not infer a line from partial alignment. If using code, verify output dimensions and all cells outside predicted changes.
4. Treat demos and wrong submissions as equal-cost actions. Request a demo only when it can distinguish live hypotheses. Before submitting, apply the validated rule to every relevant test object and preserve untouched cells.
5. On incorrect feedback, discard or materially revise the hypothesis by comparing the rejected output with every demo; do not submit an unsupported small variation. If uncertainty remains, request a discriminating demo rather than cycling guesses, within the remaining budget.
6. Stop only when the instance reports success/over or the attempt cap is reached; use `finish` only when allowed by the protocol.

# Continual-ARC task-8457a781 (solved)

## Confirmed rule
Input is a grid of background color 4, separator lines in color 1, and scattered noise/marks. Recolor the separator lines to color 2. Separator rows/columns can be detected by their uniformity: full horizontal rows consisting entirely of 1s are changed to all 2s; full vertical columns consisting entirely of 1s are changed to all 2s. Leave all other cells unchanged, including other 1s. Preserve grid dimensions.

Test was 14x24. Entire 1 rows were rows 3, 7, 10 (1-based); full 1 columns were 3, 16, 22, 24 (1-based). There was also a column of mostly 1s, e.g. col18/19, but they were NOT separator lines: retain their 1s and non-1s. Correct output changed only separator lines to 2. First two guesses failed because they incorrectly selected column 3 and 16 but missed full 1 separator columns 22 and 24 (and then guessed lines incorrectly); the final answer correctly distinguished complete solid separator lines from intermittent nearby columns.

## Demonstrations
Demo 1: 23x30 with full 0 separator lines; output recolors complete 0 rows/columns to 2. Full separator rows 4,23 and full cols 7,29,30; preserve all else.
Demo 2: 15x17 with full 1 separators; output changes full 1 separator lines to 2. Full rows 7,10,15 and col15; preserve other cells.

Task type can recur with different background/separator values. Identify the uniform full-length line(s) forming the grid dividers and recolor those line cells to 2. Confirm the line is uniformly the separator color along its entire span; do not mistake columns mostly constant for separators.
